title: Dominic and the Compass
premise: In the winter of 1893, widowed lighthouse keeper Petra Kavanagh tends the light on a storm-battered headland while her late husband's unfinished brass compass sits half-made in his workshop. When the season's first great storms destroy the only bridge to the mainland, Petra is stranded with her prickly father-in-law Alistair, who arrives carrying orders that the workshop land be sold and cleared by spring. As storms close in, Petra and Alistair must finish the compass — an inheritance meant for her son — while uncovering the truth about why her husband Dominic never completed it: he had learned the compass was commissioned to guide wreckers' ships onto the rocks. The novel ends in spring, when the bridge reopens, Petra chooses truth over loyalty to Dominic's memory by testifying against the wrecker ring, and she lights the lamp herself as keeper in her own name.
about_author: Emrys Amberdale is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the northern coast. Their fiction draws on salvaged letters, tide tables, and the quiet stubbornness of people who live where the land ends.

chapters.title: The Weight of What Stays
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Establishing the lighthouse routine one year after Dominic's drowning; she measures grief in objects that can be carried. She finds his unfinished compass wrapped in oilcloth. Emotional beat: tender numbness, the discipline of keeping the light for strangers while her own world went dark.

chapters.title: Orders from the Mainland
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A ferryman delivers papers: the workshop land has been willed into dispute, and surveyors will come at spring thaw unless the estate is settled. Petra realizes the compass may be evidence of something. Beat: unease beneath competence; the first crack in her tidy mourning.

chapters.title: Alistair Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Alistair's POV. Dominic's father arrives uninvited, cold and formal, claiming the right to oversee the workshop before it's cleared. He and Petra circle each other like weather fronts. Beat: two grieving people armed with etiquette instead of honesty.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The great storm season begins early; the bridge is condemned and closed until spring. Trapped together, they strike a bargain: finish the compass before the surveyors come, then part forever. Beat: reluctant alliance forged out of necessity.

chapters.title: What the Workshop Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Inventorying Dominic's tools, they find ledgers with payments from a shipping firm Petra doesn't recognize. Alistair insists it's nothing; Petra keeps the page. Beat: suspicion planted; the workshop becomes a room of questions.

chapters.title: Brass and Memory
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Learning the craft from Alistair's grudging instruction, she begins shaping the compass card. Working metal, she remembers Dominic teaching their son Tomas to hold a chisel. Beat: grief transmuted into craft; warmth kindling between enemies-by-circumstance.

chapters.title: The Wrecker's Light
chapters.summary: Alistair's POV. Flashback chapters within his narration reveal the shipping firm paid for false lights during wrecks decades ago — and that Dominic discovered it. Alistair came not to clear the workshop but to bury what Dominic found. Beat: guilt wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: Tomas Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Ten-year-old Tomas finds the ledger and asks why his father took money from wreckers. Petra defends Dominic instinctively, lying to her son for the first time. Beat: loyalty vs. truth turns intimate; the lie costs her something immediately.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The worst storm system of the season builds offshore; supply boat fails to run. They batten down, and Alistair nearly confesses twice and doesn't. Beat: dread accumulating like pressure before a front.

chapters.title: The Night of the Great Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The storm strikes; the light must be kept through the night, and the workshop roof tears loose. Sheltering together, Alistair finally tells Petra part of the truth: Dominic was going to testify before he drowned. Beat: terror, exhaustion, and the shattering of Petra's image of her husband.

chapters.title: Drowned or Silenced
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Reexamining the night Dominic died, Petra finds his boat's fittings were cut, not worn. Was it the sea, or the men he threatened to expose? Beat: horror sharpening into resolve; mourning becomes investigation.

chapters.title: The Commission Letter
chapters.summary: Alistair's POV. He produces Dominic's hidden letter: the compass itself was commissioned by the wreckers as a navigational gift — a bribe and a trap. Finishing it means completing a criminal's instrument. Beat: moral crisis; the inheritance is poisoned.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Petra and Alistair argue over whether to finish, destroy, or alter the compass. Petra proposes finishing it but making it tell the truth — engraving the wreckers' names inside the case. Beat: the theme crystallizes; loyalty to memory means honoring what Dominic tried to do, not what he was forced toward.

chapters.title: The Firm Sends Someone
chapters.summary: New POV: Mr. Calloway, the firm's agent, arrives by dinghy ahead of the thaw, ostensibly to help, actually to retrieve the ledgers and the compass. His courtesy is a blade. Beat: menace enters the house wearing gloves.

chapters.title: Houseguest
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Days of cat-and-mouse; Calloway inspects the workshop, praises the compass, offers Petra money and passage away. She smiles and hides the finished card in Tomas's toy chest. Beat: suppressed fear; Petra discovers she can perform composure under threat.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Lamp Room
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The boy, sensing danger, moves the ledgers into the lamp room and nearly gets caught by Calloway. His small heroism forces the adults' hands. Beat: courage inherited; the next generation acts on truth the adults have been managing.

chapters.title: Calloway's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. With the bridge still shut, he decides to burn the workshop and blame storm damage, waiting for a windy night. Beat: cold escalation; the reader sees the clock running out.

chapters.title: Fire Watch
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra catches Calloway with lantern oil; confrontation in the workshop as wind rises. Alistair takes a blow protecting the compass; Calloway flees into the storm rather than face a keeper's testimony. Beat: climax of physical danger; the family bleeds for the truth.

chapters.title: Engraving the Names
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Through the storm's aftermath, Petra and a recovering Alistair finish the compass together, engraving every wrecker payment and name inside the case — the instrument now a witness. Beat: quiet, sacred labor; grief and love reconciled in craft.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Spring thaw; the magistrate and surveyors cross with the first cart. Petra surrenders the ledgers and the compass. Calloway is taken on the mainland road. Beat: vindication without triumph; justice arriving on ordinary wheels.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the mainland courtroom, Petra testifies to what Dominic found and died for, choosing truth over the gentler memory. Alistair stands beside her, publicly naming his own years of silence. Beat: catharsis; loyalty redefined as fidelity to truth.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Light
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Back home, Petra is appointed keeper in her own name. She sets the finished compass on the mantel, opens to the engraved names, and Tomas asks to learn the trade. Final beat: inheritance restored — not objects carried, but truth kept, like a light, lit each night.
